rows.subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
rows.subtype: Approach: reading the rules and working backward from the deadline [Thinking]
rows.description: A team reads the competition rules and dates, then counts backward from the event to set milestones for design, build, testing and rehearsal, leaving a final week free.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: brainstorming, contingency planning, experiment and measure, mental simulation, minimum viable version

rows.subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
rows.subtype: Approach: brainstorming many ideas then selecting one [Thinking]
rows.description: Team members write twenty possible robot designs on sticky notes without judging, then vote using cost, time and skill criteria, and choose a simple line-follower with a clever sensor arrangement.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, experiment and measure, mental simulation, minimum viable version, working backward

rows.subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
rows.subtype: Approach: building a minimum working prototype first [Action]
rows.description: The team builds a basic chassis that moves and turns before adding sensors, so each new part is tested on something that already works and faults are easy to trace.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: brainstorming, contingency planning, experiment and measure, mental simulation, working backward

rows.subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
rows.subtype: Approach: testing repeatedly and logging failures [Action]
rows.description: Students run the robot fifty times on a mock track, record each failure and its cause in a log, and fix the most frequent problem first, such as a loose wheel or sensor glare.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: brainstorming, contingency planning, experiment and measure, mental simulation, minimum viable version, working backward

rows.subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
rows.description: One student handles wiring, another coding, another documentation and presentation, and they swap ideas at weekly meetings, using individual strengths while keeping shared understanding.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: brainstorming, contingency planning, experiment and measure, mental simulation, minimum viable version, working backward

rows.subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
rows.subtype: Approach: last-minute changes before the event [Pitfall]
rows.description: The night before, the team rewrites the control code to add a new feature, never tests it fully, and the robot misbehaves in the first round, showing the risk of untested changes.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: brainstorming, contingency planning, mental simulation, minimum viable version, working backward

rows.subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
rows.subtype: Approach: one strong member doing everything [Pitfall]
rows.description: A gifted teen builds the whole project alone because it is quicker, and when he falls ill on the day, teammates cannot operate or explain it, since knowledge was never shared.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: brainstorming, contingency planning, experiment and measure, mental simulation, minimum viable version, working backward

rows.subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
rows.subtype: Approach: contingency plan with spare parts [Thinking]
rows.description: The team packs spare batteries, sensors, wires and tools, and assigns one member to repair, so a broken part on the day is an inconvenience rather than the end of the run.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: brainstorming, experiment and measure, mental simulation, minimum viable version, working backward

rows.subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
rows.subtype: Approach: reviewing the result and learning from the loss [Revision]
rows.description: After finishing fifth, the team meets, lists what went well and what failed, such as poor calibration, and writes changes for the next year, treating the result as feedback rather than a verdict.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: brainstorming, contingency planning, experiment and measure, mental simulation, minimum viable version, working backward

rows.subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
rows.subtype: Approach: rehearsing the presentation to judges [Action]
rows.description: Students practise explaining their design in three minutes to a teacher and parents, refine unclear parts after questions, and prepare answers for likely questions about cost and safety.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: brainstorming, contingency planning, experiment and measure, minimum viable version, working backward
